title: Tata Sons forced to list, rupee at 95.5 and bond yields past 7 percent cap a fifth losing week for Dalal Street
standfirst: Indian equities ended a fifth straight losing week with the Nifty at 23,398 and the Sensex at 74,782, as Brent crude above 104 dollars and US Treasury yields near 5 percent kept investors on the back foot. The RBI rejected Tata Sons' bid to stay unlisted, SEBI moved to rework the closing auction session, and HDFC Bank named two candidates for its next chief. Globally, hot US inflation cemented bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike next week, Saudi Arabia shut its pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, and BRICS leaders in New Delhi agreed a joint declaration despite Gulf tensions.

items.text: The Nifty closed Friday at 23,398.10 and the Sensex at 74,781.76, down 2.1 percent and 2.3 percent for the week, a fifth straight weekly loss driven by crude oil and rising US bond yields. Technical analysts say the Nifty's break below the 23,900 to 24,000 zone turns that area into resistance.
The rupee ended the week at 95.54 to the dollar after its sharpest weekly fall in four months, as Brent held above 104 dollars on Strait of Hormuz tensions.
India's 10-year government bond yield crossed 7 percent after the RBI accepted less than half the amount it targeted at a three-year bond auction, raising the cost of government borrowing.
Foreign ownership of Indian-listed companies has slipped to a 17-year low as global funds chase the AI boom elsewhere and Indian earnings stay muted.

Wall Street rose on Friday despite hot inflation data, with the Dow up about 1 percent to 52,573 and the S&P 500 at 7,656.98, while Brent slipped 2.8 percent to 104.61 dollars but finished the week up 9.5 percent. The US 10-year yield closed at 4.97 percent.

The RBI rejected Tata Sons' request to surrender its NBFC registration, forcing the Rs 2.01 lakh crore holding company toward a stock market listing within three years. Sources say Tata Sons will try to renegotiate with the RBI before considering any legal step.

SEBI issued a consultation paper on the closing auction session with two options for expiry-day derivatives settlement, two alternatives for market timings and changes to order cancellation and Iceberg orders, after a month of volatile expiry sessions.
HDFC Bank's board sent two names to the RBI for the MD and CEO role, reportedly including internal candidate Kaizad Bharucha, and appointed chief credit officer Jimmy Tata as executive director.
Finance Minister Sitharaman pushed the RBI to speed up digital rupee pilots and tokenisation with light-touch rules, and met the AIIB president to discuss local-currency financing for infrastructure.

The RBI published draft KYC amendments and a standard procedure for freezing money-mule accounts after a Supreme Court order, while the US finalised anti-dumping and countervailing duties on Indian solar cells and panels.

US consumer prices accelerated in August with the biggest core rise in four months, pushing the odds of a quarter-point Fed hike at next week's meeting to about 90 percent. The WSJ notes a first Fed hike rarely comes alone.
Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline, the route it has used to bypass the closed Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks it blamed on militants in Iraq, tightening global oil supply.

BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration by consensus despite Iran-UAE divisions over the Gulf conflict, opposing carbon border taxes, pushing local-currency payments and backing a grain exchange. Modi and Xi agreed to work on the border dispute and trade imbalance.

ECB policymaker Kaasik said it is understandable that markets expect more European rate hikes, adding to the global tightening mood, while Canada courts up to 1 trillion dollars from investors seeking shelter from US trade policy.

watch: The US Federal Reserve's September 16-17 meeting, where a quarter-point hike is now priced at about 90 percent.
Indian markets are shut Monday 14 September for Ganesh Chaturthi; trading resumes Tuesday with the Tata Sons listing overhang and SEBI's closing auction consultation in play.
Brent crude above 104 dollars with both the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline disrupted; the rupee near 95.5 and the 10-year yield above 7 percent.
Whether the Nifty can reclaim the 23,900 to 24,000 zone that has turned into resistance after a fifth losing week.
